conclusion: Version 1.3 uses a five-word, 0x14-byte internal command record in a 32-slot modulo ring at 0x83155C28. Drain function 0x82CE16C8 copies one record and directly calls dispatcher 0x82CDDF08. The dispatcher reads type plus three arguments, accepts unsigned types 0 through 65, and branches through the exact 66-entry table at 0x82CDE014. Submit function 0x82CE1950 keeps its target argument separate, copies the five-word record into a distinct vtable-bearing object through 0x82D90A18, and routes it through a network-manager child. Numeric type 49 has the neutral static role of ORing a LocalPlayerIdResolve-derived slw mask into 0x83157E44; cases 46 and 47 initialize that mask and contain three exact type-49 submit sites, while case 46 later compares it with the human-player mask. No original turn/synchronization name or runtime barrier follows. The command object's paired methods serialize and deserialize the embedded record as five ordered 32-bit primitives for an exact 20-byte object-layer payload with conditional byte-order conversion. The factory pointer's initialized row belongs to executable-wide function metadata, not a network registry, and no supported static consumer maps outbound leading value 77 to the factory. Outer framing, target encoding, platform transport, runtime delivery, and unsupported cross-platform semantics remain unresolved.
